answers.question: A review found that the rule on reads presents the end of a read that never answers as settled, though you left it open, and that the agent's message when the first read of your orders fails is in no rule. I propose this change to rule R-13. Before: "When a read gets no answer, the agent sends it again; the owner set no limit on reads. Only a read that fails with an error counts as a failed read." After: "When a read gets no answer, the agent sends it again; the owner set no limit on reads, so what ends a read that never answers is an open question. Only a read that fails with an error counts as a failed read. When the first read of the customer's orders fails with an error, the agent says it cannot see their orders right now and changes nothing." Do you accept the change?
answers.recommended: Yes: apply the change to R-13.
answers.reply:
Yes, I accept your recommendation.
> Reads may be retried on timeout without limit; only commit calls are bounded.

answers.question: A review found that no rule says one proposal covers one order, though you accepted that each proposal cancels one order and another order needs its own proposal and yes. I propose this change to rule R-05. Before: "The agent states one proposal: cancel this whole order, and refund its total paid to the order's payment method. It cancels only after the customer clearly says yes to that proposal." After: "The agent states one proposal: cancel this whole order, and refund its total paid to the order's payment method. One proposal cancels one order; another order gets its own proposal and its own yes. It cancels only after the customer clearly says yes to that proposal." The rest of R-05 stays as it is. Do you accept the change?
answers.recommended: Yes: apply the change to R-05.
answers.reply:
Yes, I accept your recommendation.
> Proposed default: the agent cancels an order only after the customer explicitly confirms the full proposal (which order, the refund amount and where it goes); any change after confirmation voids it.
> Proposed: the agent states one proposal (e.g. "cancel order HG-10482 and refund $86.40 to Visa ending 4242"); the customer's one "yes" authorizes both calls.

answers.question: A review found that rule R-08 says "an error" where it means only a transient error, so a reader could expect a retry after a terminal one. I propose this change to rule R-08. Before: "After a refund call that answers with an error or gets no answer, the agent sends the refund call once more; it sends at most two refund calls for one order. After a failed refund, or an answer that the order is not cancelled, it sends none." After: "After a refund call that answers with a passing (transient) error or gets no answer, the agent sends the refund call once more; it sends at most two refund calls for one order. After a failed refund (a lasting, terminal error), or an answer that the order is not cancelled, it sends none." The rest of R-08 stays as it is. Do you accept the change?
answers.recommended: Yes: apply the change to R-08.
answers.reply:
> One retry allowed on a transient error, none on a terminal one.
> Proposed: transient = payment provider temporarily unavailable, retry once; terminal = payment method can no longer receive money (card closed or expired) or the provider declines, no retry, hand off.
> Proposed set shown to the user: list_orders() (returns each order with its refund or null), cancel_order(order_number), issue_refund(order_number) (supplied), request_staff_followup(order_number, reason) with reasons refund_not_issued, refund_status_unknown, cancellation_unknown; terminal refund error returns a refund with status failed, transient error creates none; handoff timeout not retried; SG-02 (store staff work every follow-up task) added.
